newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FERC approves Lilco, Brooklyn Union merger.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FERC approves Lilco, Brooklyn Union merger.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission on Wednesday approved the merger of Long Island Lighting Co with Brooklyn Union Gas Co .

The merger would create a $4 billion electric and gas company, including all of Brooklyn Union's operations and Lilco's natural gas system, non-nuclear power generating assets and certain other assets and about 2.2 million customers in three New York City boroughs and Long Island.

Under the deal, subject to state approval, the New York's Long Island Power Authority will buy Lilco's electric transmission and distribution system and its share of the upstate Nine Mile Point 2 nuclear plant.
LIPA will also assume or refinance $3.6 billion of Lilco's $4.5 billion debt, largely linked to the Shoreham nuclear plant, which never opened.
